title: Rigveda 9.43: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.43: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.43 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 683r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.43.1-6 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 33); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 683r
translation.original_text:
1yo atya̍ iva mṛ̱jyate̱ gobhi̱r madā̍ya harya̱taḥ | taṁ gī̱rbhir vā̍sayāmasi ||
2taṁ no̱ viśvā̍ ava̱syuvo̱ gira̍ḥ śumbhanti pū̱rvathā̍ | indu̱m indrā̍ya pī̱taye̍ ||
3pu̱nā̱no yā̍ti harya̱taḥ somo̍ gī̱rbhiḥ pari̍ṣkṛtaḥ | vipra̍sya̱ medhyā̍titheḥ ||
4pava̍māna vi̱dā ra̱yim a̱smabhya̍ṁ soma su̱śriya̍m | indo̍ sa̱hasra̍varcasam ||
5indu̱r atyo̱ na vā̍ja̱sṛt kani̍kranti pa̱vitra̱ ā | yad akṣā̱r ati̍ deva̱yuḥ ||
6pava̍sva̱ vāja̍sātaye̱ vipra̍sya gṛṇa̱to vṛ̱dhe | soma̱ rāsva̍ su̱vīrya̍m ||
translation.text:
1WE will enrobe with sacred song the Lovely One who, as a Steed, Is decked with milk for rapturous joy.
2All songs of ours desiring grace adorn him in the ancient way, Indu for Indra, for his drink.
3Soma flows on when purified, beloved and adorned with songs, Songs of the sage Medhyâtithi.
4O Soma Pavamâna, find exceeding glorious wealth for us, Wealth, Indu, fraught with boundless might.
5Like courser racing to the prize Indu, the lover of the Gods, Roars, as he passes, in the sieve.
6Flow on thy way to win us strength, to speed the sage who praises thee: Soma, bestow heroic power.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 683r (numbered 105r by the scribe) (OPenn image 683, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.42.5 ‹abhi viśvāni vāryā abhi›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 684v (numbered 1v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.44.1 ‹pra naḥ indo iti›. Verses 9.43.1-6 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1yaḥ | atyaḥ-iva | mṛjyate | gobhiḥ | madāya | haryataḥ | tam | gīḥ-bhiḥ | vāsayāmasi
2tam | naḥ | viśvāḥ | avasyuvaḥ | giraḥ | śumbhanti | pūrva-thā | indum | indrāya | pītaye
3punānaḥ | yāti | haryataḥ | somaḥ | gīḥ-bhiḥ | pari-kṛtaḥ | viprasya | medhya-atitheḥ
4pavamāna | vidāḥ | rayim | asmabhyam | soma | su-śriyam | indo iti | sahasra-varcasam
5induḥ | atyaḥ | na | vāja-sṛt | kanikranti | pavitre | ā | yat | akṣāḥ | ati | deva-yuḥ
6pavasva | vāja-sātaye | viprasya | gṛṇataḥ | vṛdhe | soma | rāsva | su-vīryam
